title: Incident-to-SLO Feedback Loop: Campaign Plan & Tactics
content:
Purpose:
This is a 90-day cross-functional campaign to close the loop between production incidents and SLO evolution. Instead of treating SLOs as static artifacts, we will treat incidents as raw signals that should inform: alert thresholds, SLO definitions, alerting playbooks, and product communications. The campaign focuses on operationalizing a repeatable feedback loop so SLO maintenance is continuous, measurable, and distributed across teams.

Background and motivation:
- We have recurring model-serving latency spikes that pass through downstream caching layers, creating intermittent user impact not well captured by current p95/p99 SLOs.
- Postmortems frequently call out unclear alert ownership and SLOs that were either too coarse or misaligned with customer impact.
- Goal: reduce time between incident detection and SLO/action change to <= 21 days for prioritized incidents.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Establish a documented Incident->SLO decision flow and decision record for each prioritized incident class.
2) Deliver 6 tactical SLO/alert adjustments across serving/runtime/ingestion by the end of the 90-day window.
3) Automate one metric extraction pipeline that converts key postmortem signals into SLO candidate metrics.
4) Reduce repeated incident recurrence rate for the top-3 incident classes by 30%.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: model-serving latency & availability incidents, cache invalidation patterns, autoscaling misconfigurations, and alert fatigue related to these classes.
- Out-of-scope: client-side SDK bugs, billing/quotas, and infra provisioning incidents handled by separate oncall teams.

Hypothesis to validate:
If we create a low-friction path from postmortem evidence -> SLO candidate -> A/B rollouts of alert/SLO changes with monitoring bake time, then SLOs will better reflect user impact and reduce repeated incidents due to misconfigured signals.

Success metrics (how we will judge progress):
- Decision latency: median time from incident close to SLO decision recorded (target <= 21 days).
- Change throughput: number of SLO/alert adjustments merged and deployed (target >= 6).
- Recurrence reduction: % fewer repeats in prioritized incident classes (target 30% reduction).
- Post-change signal quality: reduction in false-positive alerts for adjusted alerts (target 40% fewer noisy alerts).

Workstreams and key activities (owners listed):
1) Detection & signals hygiene (owner: Jia Chen)
   - Inventory noisy alerts and annotate with recent postmortem links.
   - Implement a tagging convention in metrics repo for incident-related metrics (inc_class, root_cause_tag).
   - Deliverable: noisy-alerts-inventory.csv + tagging PR.

2) Postmortem -> SLO conversion playbook (owner: Priya Nair)
   - Create a lightweight template that extracts: impact windows, user-visible symptoms, metric pivots, and suggested SLO dimensions.
   - Run pilot on last 6 incidents and produce SLO candidate list.
   - Deliverable: incident-to-slo-template.md + candidate roster.

3) SLO design & rollout (owner: Liam O'Connor)
   - Define SLO change experiment protocol: canary targets, rollback criteria, monitoring bake time.
   - Execute 6 change experiments across serving/runtime teams.
   - Deliverable: SLO-change-playbook + change PRs.

4) Alerts tuning & runbooks (owner: María Gómez)
   - For each SLO change, align alert thresholds and runbook steps.
   - Reduce duplicate alerts; consolidate to owner-aware channels.
   - Deliverable: updated runbooks + alert config patches.

5) Automation & tooling (owner: Noah Patel)
   - Build a simple pipeline: postmortem metadata -> SLO candidate dashboard.
   - Prototype a dashboard that surfaces candidate SLOs and expected impact.
   - Deliverable: dashboard prototype + ingestion job.

6) Product & CS alignment (owner: Ava Martinez)
   - Host two working sessions with Product and CS to validate user-impact assumptions for SLO proposals.
   - Get explicit acceptance for proposed SLO changes that adjust customer-facing expectations.
   - Deliverable: acceptance notes + comms plan.

Timeline (90-day, calendarized):
- Week 0 (kickoff): stakeholder alignment, owners assigned, baseline metrics captured.
- Weeks 1-2: noisy-alert inventory, postmortem template draft, tooling discovery.
- Weeks 3-5: pilot conversions (3 incidents), dashboard alpha, first SLO candidate proposals.
- Weeks 6-9: execute first 3 SLO change experiments + alert tuning, product acceptance sessions.
- Weeks 10-12: second set of 3 experiments, tooling hardening, runbook rollouts.
- Week 13: campaign retrospective, decision log published, next-step proposals.

Roles & RACI at a glance:
- Responsible: workstream owners above.
- Accountable: Priya Nair (campaign lead).
- Consulted: product managers for impacted features, customer-success for impact validation.
- Informed: Platform Eng, SRE oncall rotation, Exec reliability updates.

Required artifacts and places to record decisions:
- Incident->SLO decision log (Confluence page): template will link SLO candidates to incident evidence and final decision rationale.
- SLO change PRs in infra and observability repos (link in tickets).
- Runbook edits in runbooks repo.

Meeting cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync: progress, blockers, decision review.
- Biweekly SLO approval session (30-60m) with Product & CS.
- Monthly demo to Reliability Council.

Quick checklists (for each incident class we act on):
- [ ] Map incident to user-visible impact and quantify affected time/users.
- [ ] Extract candidate metrics and propose SLO dimension (endpoint-level, cluster-level, or customer-level).
- [ ] Draft change experiment plan with bake time and rollback triggers.
- [ ] Notify oncall, product, CS, and platform teams.
- [ ] Deploy change in canary, monitor for bake period, then promote or rollback.
- [ ] Update postmortem with decision outcome and link to SLO change record.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overfitting SLOs to one-off incidents -> Mitigation: require recurrence evidence and N incidents or N% exposure before permanent change.
- Risk: Alert churn and fatigue from frequent experiments -> Mitigation: group changes into rolling windows and limit experiment cadence per subsystem.
- Risk: Product disagreement on customer impact -> Mitigation: require written acceptance for any change that adjusts outward-facing SLA language.

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
- What is the minimum evidence threshold (count/time window) to convert an incident into an SLO candidate?
- Who signs off on SLO changes that touch enterprise customer contracts?
- Can we add a label to postmortem templates that auto-creates an SLO candidate in tooling?

Appendix (templates & example):
- Incident->SLO template (example fields): incident id, date, user impact summary, affected endpoints, candidate metric + query, proposed SLO (window & target), rollout plan, expected tradeoffs.
- Example: Incident #2026-0112: "KV cache evictions spike" -> candidate SLO: endpoint-serve-latency.p95 < 300ms over 1m window for production-serving cluster.

Next steps (first 7 days):
- Priya: publish this doc to Confluence and create decision-log page.
- Jia: start noisy-alert inventory and share CSV by EOD week 1.
- Liam: draft SLO-change-playbook skeleton and example experiment protocol.
- María: inventory runbooks tied to top-3 incident classes.
- Noah: prototype minimal ingestion pipeline to tag postmortems.

Notes to self (working thoughts):
- Keep experiments small and reversible. Aim for clear rollback criteria.
- Prefer alert de-dup and owner routing over creating more alerts.
- Champion tooling that nudges teams to revisit SLOs quarterly instead of annually.

End of draft.
